title: Normalized finite scalar and etale-origin transport to constant coefficient modules
statement: Use constant-coefficient module sheaves and strict towers [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], with exact open extension [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Let $\varphi:B\to\Lambda$ be a ring homomorphism to a finite commutative ring. Realize fixed $\Lambda$-module pro-etale sheaves as modules over the continuous-function finite coefficient sheaf [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], then restrict scalars along the canonical map sending $b$ to the constant function $\varphi(b)$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Call this exact functor $C_X$. Its underlying additive sheaf comparison is normalized to send each sheafification-unit section to itself. The direct-image comparison is the unique isomorphism acting identically on the same pulled-back sections under this identification. Put $H_X= C_X\nu_X^*$ for the canonical etale/pro-etale inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The comparison $H_Y f_*^{et}\to f_* H_X$ is the composite of the mate of the canonical site pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] and the preceding sectionwise scalar comparison. Its inverse mate defines the inverse-image comparison, and the inverse of the open-adjunction inverse mate defines the forward open-extension comparison; the derived direct-image comparison is the right-derived unit-normalized descent of this same arrow. For an unbounded derived constant-coefficient module $K$, a scalar etale origin consists of such a ring $\Lambda$, map $\varphi$, a bounded-below finite-coefficient object with its recorded etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], and an isomorphism from its scalar restriction to $K$. Forgetting commutativity from commutative ring sheaves to ring sheaves commutes with sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], with its canonical unit-preserving comparison.

The source states the etale result; the tower realization, finite-evaluation normalization and pro-etale extension are additional assertions to be proved, not quotations from the source.; strict-tower proof steps introducing these operations.

proof.text: Restrict a module over the constant commutative ring sheaf along the unit from the constant B presheaf. This produces a sheaf of fixed B-modules. Local bijectivity of the unit makes this functor fully faithful and essentially surjective: lift morphisms by local surjectivity and sheafify a fixed-module presheaf for essential surjectivity. The sheafification unit is invertible because its underlying additive presheaf is already a sheaf. This is an equivalence for arbitrary B, including the zero ring.

Linearize cUnderlying using its scalar-unit normalization to identify C followed by the preceding equivalence with ordinary restriction of scalars. Direct image followed by this equivalence is sectionwise identical to the fixed-B direct image. The defining cDirect normalization identifies the pasted direct-image square with the restriction-of-scalars square. Injectivity and horizontal/vertical pasting for mateEquiv identify the corresponding pullback squares. Mates across equivalences preserve isomorphisms, so the original coefficient pullback square is invertible.

For an open immersion, identify upperStar with ordinary open restriction by the canonical localization isomorphism. The mate of the identity restriction/scalar square under restriction/direct-image adjunctions is the identity, by the triangle equation. Uniqueness of mates identifies its transported square with upperStarRestrictScalarsIso. Its open-extension mate is openExtensionScalarMap, invertible by the scalar extension-by-zero comparison. The open-unit normalization similarly identifies the site pullback square with the mate of the canonical extension comparison. Paste these open mates. Cancel the equivalence square to obtain invertibility of the coefficient open mate, and then paste with the site mate to prove hOpenInv_isIso for the specified transformation.

Identify the site part of hDirect with lowerStarComparisonUpperStarBaseChange by twice taking mates and applying the conjugation identity. This map is invertible for qcqs morphisms by the source cohomology-continuity comparison. Together with cDirect this proves that hDirect itself is invertible.

A generic equivalence square transports classical higher direct images: use rightDerivedCompObjIso, rightDerivedObjIsoOfIso, and compRightDerivedObjIso on injective resolutions; equivalences are exact and preserve injectives. Faithfulness and additivity reflect the vanishing of the resulting higher direct images. An injective etale sheaf becomes direct-image acyclic under site inverse image for qcqs morphisms. The source rightDerivedLowerStarRestrictScalarsIso transports this acyclicity through scalar restriction, and the constant-ring equivalence reflects it to module sheaves. Therefore H sends injectives to module-direct-image acyclic objects. Apply the acyclic-object criterion to hDirect and compose with the compatibility isomorphisms in hR to obtain hR_isIso.
